content.overview: BNS s. 215 — Refusing to sign statement.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Refusing to sign statement. BNS restatement of IPC 181. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 181. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 215 is the rule on “Refusing to sign statement”. The section provides that whoever refuses to sign any statement made by him, when required to sign that statement by a public servant legally competent to require that he shall sign that statement, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to three thousand rupees, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 215 exists so that “Refusing to sign statement” has a closed legal test in Chapter XIII — Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Summons, proclamations, false information — and the recast suicide-attempt-to-coerce offence.
